title: Questions and Answers on the Compiled Edition of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life
author: Zhanran
excerpt: Master Lianchi said of the compiled edition: "It has been of great service to the Pure Land."

inline.s: Master Lianchi said of the compiled edition: "It has been of great service to the Pure Land."
Master Ouyi said of the compiled edition: "This is the wheel of Dharmakara's vows."
Moreover, Wang Longshu's compiled edition was included in the Qianlong Tripitaka.
Recite it always, hear it always; remember it always, practice it always,
so that body and mind enter ever more deeply into Ultimate Bliss, and come ever nearer to Ultimate Bliss.
Though one strives and toils with zeal for a lifetime long, it is but a moment's space;
then one is born in the Land of Immeasurable Life, where bliss knows no bounds.
Good and evil, when their end arrives, always meet their retribution; three feet above your head, the gods are watching.
Question: Why should the Sutra of Immeasurable Life be compiled?
Answer:
To compile the Sutra of Immeasurable Life
is a practical need in the study and practice of the Pure Land school

. The Sutra of Immeasurable Life is the essence of the whole body of Pure Land scriptures: it sets out in detail the causal ground and the fruition of Amitābha Buddha's attainment of Buddhahood, the splendor of the land and of its inhabitants in the Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, the faith, vows, practice, and realization of the sentient beings who attain rebirth there, and the Pure Land practitioner's yearning for that land and detachment from samsara.

This is a scripture that those who recite the Buddha's name must constantly read and steep themselves in, so that body and mind may enter ever more deeply into Ultimate Bliss and come ever nearer to Ultimate Bliss.
But because this sutra has five translations whose contents are not entirely the same, it is hard for those who recite the Buddha's name to recite and steep themselves in them all regularly.

[That it is hard for those who recite the Buddha's name to recite and steep themselves in them all] Just look at how many of those who recite the Buddha's name have recited all five of these original translations through, or even recite all five of them regularly, and you will know. The difficulty of reciting them all is far greater than you imagine! Just read the five original translations through for yourself
(to read and recite them, please click
The Five Original Translations of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life
, and it will be clear.
You will then also understand the
necessity
and
urgency
of compiling the Sutra of Immeasurable Life.
These five translations
(see
The Five Original Translations of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life
are:
1. The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha of Immeasurable Purity, Equality, and Enlightenment (Han Translation)
2. The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on Amitābha, the Perfectly Enlightened One, and the Deliverance of Human Beings (Wu Translation)
3. The Sutra of Immeasurable Life Spoken by the Buddha (Wei Translation)
4. The Assembly of the Tathagata of Immeasurable Life (Tang Translation)
5. The Sutra of the Adornments of the Mahayana Immeasurable Life of the Buddha (Song Translation).
Thus, one after another, such great masters as Wang Longshu, Peng Shaosheng,
Wei Chengguan,
and Xia Lianju aroused the aspiration to take the
contents
of the five original translations and compile (synthesize) them together, using refined and concise wording to
expound
and
spread
these five original translations, so as to aid daily
steeping in them:
to grasp the meaning of the sutra
(the meaning of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life)
, deepen faith and vows, and cultivate in accordance with the teaching.
Therefore,
a compiled edition is not a Buddhist sutra, nor is it a stringing together of the words and phrases of sutras, but an exposition of the sutras; hence
Master Ouyi praised it, saying:
"This is the wheel of Dharmakara's vows."
These four compiled editions are:
1. The Great Amitābha Sutra, Song dynasty
compiled by Wang Rixiu (Wang Longshu); briefly called the "Wang compiled edition of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life"
2. The Sutra of Immeasurable Life (Peng Shaosheng's Abridged and Collated Edition), early Qing dynasty
abridged and collated by Peng Shaosheng (Peng Jiqing, Peng Erlin) on the basis of the Wei translation; briefly called the "Peng compiled edition of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life"
3. The Maha Amitābha Sutra, Qing dynasty, Xianfeng era
compiled by Wei Yuan (Wei Chengguan, Wei Moshen); briefly called the "Wei compiled edition of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life"
4. The Mahayana Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Adornments of Immeasurable Life, Purity, Equality, and Enlightenment, Republic of China period
compiled by Xia Lianju; briefly called the "Xia compiled edition of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life".

Of the four compiled editions, the Xia edition is the best. Its merits are these: building on the three earlier compiled editions, it develops their strengths and makes up for their shortcomings, and it makes a fine compilation of the five original translations; moreover, its wording and meaning are clear, elegant, and fluent, easy to recite and easy to remember, and especially suited to the study and practice of ordinary people who recite the Buddha's name.

[That it makes a fine compilation of the five original translations] Readers may put themselves in another's place and consider: if you were a teaching master and now had to synthesize the contents of the five original translations and expound them, how well would you do? Then you would know how very difficult this Compiled Edition was to accomplish, and that it is the devoted labor of those who spread the Dharma.
Question: May the Sutra of Immeasurable Life be compiled? May it be compiled by a layman?
Answer: The Sutra of Immeasurable Life may be compiled, and it may be compiled by a layman.
Wang Longshu's passing away while standing
, that sublime and auspicious sign,
together with the exceedingly high praise that patriarchs and great masters have bestowed on him through the ages,
as well as
Wang Longshu's compiled edition of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life
(the Great Amitābha Sutra)
being included in the Qianlong Tripitaka (the Dragon Canon),
all of this
proves
that the Sutra of Immeasurable Life
may be compiled, and may be compiled by a layman
As for the exceedingly high praise that patriarchs and great masters have given Wang Longshu through the ages, a few examples follow:
Master Ouyi collated and wrote a preface for Wang Longshu's compiled edition, the Great Amitābha Sutra, calling it
"the wheel of Dharmakara's vows"
, and
strenuously
promoted its circulation
. Master Ouyi said:
"In the Song dynasty there was
(that is, the Song dynasty)
the layman Wang Longshu, who had not seen the excellent recension in the Ratnakuta,
(he had not seen the translation called the Assembly of the Tathagata of Immeasurable Life in the Maharatnakuta Sutra)
and so gathered the four translations
(that is, he used the other four translations)
, discarding what was weak and taking what was strong, and named it the Great Amitābha Sutra.
It has circulated throughout the world for more than a thousand years

. The revered elder Wanrong of Shousheng Hermitage obtained an old edition from the marketplace, compared it with the northern and southern canons, found both its wording and its meaning superior, and made it public in print.
This is the wheel of Dharmakara's vows
, the same in ancient and modern times."
(from the Lingfeng Zonglun
Postface to the Engraved and Collated Great Amitābha Sutra)
In his Biography of Wang Longshu, Scholar of the Imperial College, Master Lianchi praised him, saying:
"Longshu urged people to cultivate the Western Pure Land with the utmost fervor and earnestness. He did not merely speak of it; he truly put it into practice.
And at the moment of his death he was so sublime and extraordinary that he shines through the ages.
Alas!
Was he not a sage of the Pure Land who entered the marketplace
chan
, meaning the market)
and reached down his hand
(to receive and guide sentient beings)
And he praised Wang Longshu's compiled edition in the highest terms:
"Truly, it has been of great service to the Pure Land!"
Only: "
It is to be regretted that there is much in it that is not quite right."
Master Lianchi said:
The layman's compilation of the four translations
(the layman Wang Longshu's compilation of the four original translations)
is concise in wording and complete in meaning, smooth in phrasing and clear in principle
Truly, it has been of great service to the Pure Land!
It is to be regretted that there is much in it that is not quite right
(regrettably, there is much in it that is not quite appropriate)
(from the Daily Recitation of Various Sutras)
[That there is much in it that is not quite right]
So the task of later generations
is to correct,
in this compiled edition that has been "of great service to the Pure Land",
those places where "there is much in it that is not quite right".
Please note: Master Lianchi said of the compiled edition:
"It has been of great service to the Pure Land."
Master Ouyi said of the compiled edition:
This is the wheel of Dharmakara's vows.
Moreover, Wang Longshu's compiled edition of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life
was included in the Qianlong Tripitaka
(the Dragon Canon)
In his essay In Praise of Wang Longshu, National Master Yulin says:
"Books on rebirth in the Pure Land are indeed vast in number and abundant,
but for single-mindedness in holding the name and refinement in one's practice, none surpasses Wang Longshu's Pure Land Writings!
In former days I read his book, and each time I laid down the scroll and sighed three times, wishing to circulate it widely."
Peng Shaosheng's Biography of Wang Xuzhong says:
"Xuzhong
(Wang Longshu)
once took the Sutra of Immeasurable Life and praised the Western Pure Land; its meaning is deep and vast. But from the Han to the Song
(the original translations from the Han dynasty to the Song dynasty)
the translations were obscure and blocked, seldom hitting the proper measure, so that the purport of our Buddha's teaching of the sutra was not made clear.
He therefore prayed to Avalokitesvara
and compiled the four texts into one translation. It took three years to complete, and he divided it into fifty-six sections.
Its language is refined and elegant and its order brilliantly clear, and so it came to be widely practiced in the world.
Master Yinguang praised Wang Longshu, saying:
"In the time of the Southern Song,
among the earlier worthies of our school there was the layman Longshu,
whose given name was Rixiu and whose courtesy name was Xuzhong.
He had returned by the power of his vow
(please note: Master Yinguang says that Wang Longshu was a great bodhisattva who returned by the power of his vow)
and taught the Dharma with his own person
. Though he lived amid worldly customs, he did not take a wife. Though he entered the Imperial College
(though he passed the imperial examination as a jinshi of the Imperial College)

, he did not set foot on the official career. He expounded the essential teachings of Confucianism and Buddhism and instructed his disciples who had faith. And he wished that his fellow men might all be born in the Pure Land. So he produced this book and advocated it everywhere: its words are simple yet authoritative, its principles deep yet manifest. Bending down to accord with those of lesser capacity, he led them along step by step, exhausting a grandmotherly kindness that stopped at nothing."
(from the Inscription and Preface for the Re-engraving of Longshu's Pure Land Writings)
For Wang Longshu's compiled edition of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life (the Great Amitābha Sutra), Master Ouyi personally collated and engraved it and wrote a preface in praise, saying:
It has circulated throughout the world for more than a thousand years.
This is the wheel of Dharmakara's vows.
the Lingfeng Zonglun
Postface to the Engraved and Collated Great Amitābha Sutra
) Master Yinguang said:
"The larger sutra cited in the Chao

(the Brief Explanation of the Amitābha Sutra with the Perfectly Penetrating Commentary, written by Master Youxi of the Ming dynasty and briefly called the Yuanzhong Commentary on the Amitābha Sutra, which ranks with Master Lianchi's Commentary and Notes on the Amitābha Sutra and Master Ouyi's Essential Explanation of the Amitābha Sutra as the three great commentaries on the Amitābha Sutra)
is
(the Sutra of Immeasurable Life)
namely the Great Amitābha Sutra
. Master Youxi cited it
because its wording and meaning are thorough and it has circulated throughout the world
, and so he made a point of quoting it."
(from the Preface Urging Its Practice for the Re-engraving of the Brief Explanation of the Amitābha Sutra with the Perfectly Penetrating Commentary)
Therefore,
the Sutra of Immeasurable Life may be compiled, and may be compiled by a layman
. Whether it is compiled well or not is another question, a question of how to improve it.

Xia Lianju's Compiled Edition is precisely an improvement on the three earlier compiled editions: it both adopts their strengths and avoids their errors and shortcomings, and its wording and meaning are clear, elegant, and fluent, easy to recite and easy to remember.
Question: Does reciting a compiled edition mean one will fall into hell?

Answer: That is a vicious slander of the Dharma! The compiled edition was included in the Qianlong Tripitaka, and its author, Wang Longshu, passed away standing upright and was reborn in the highest grade of the highest class; how then should those who recite a compiled edition fall into hell?

If reciting a compiled edition means falling into hell, then should those eminent monks who included the compiled edition in the Qianlong Tripitaka also fall into hell? Should Master Ouyi, who personally collated and engraved the compiled edition and wrote a preface praising it as "the wheel of Dharmakara's vows", also fall into hell? Should the author of the compiled edition, Wang Longshu, fall into hell all the more? The facts are precisely the opposite: Wang Longshu passed away standing upright and was reborn in the highest grade of the highest class! It is rather those who slander the Dharma and cut off others' wisdom-life who should be the ones to fall into hell.

Those who recite the compiled edition are grasping the meaning of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life through steeping themselves in it, deepening their faith and vows, and cultivating in accordance with the teaching. What fault could there possibly be in that? Yet for so many years it has been ceaselessly attacked, slandered, and defamed! Is this the harassment of men, or the harassment of maras? Those who do such things might well reflect: what kind of karmic retribution comes from cutting off others' roots of goodness?
Questions and Answers:
A visitor listed five reasons in opposition to compiled editions and put them forward as a challenge. For ease of reading, each is now answered in turn in the form of a note.
Before replying, one point must first be made clear: what is called compiling
is the compiling of content
(synthesizing it), that is to say, synthesizing the contents of the five original translations and using refined and concise wording to
expound and spread the Sutra of Immeasurable Life
(the five original translations as a whole), so as to aid daily
steeping in it:
grasping the meaning of the sutra
(the meaning of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life)
, deepening faith and vows, and cultivating in accordance with the teaching.
Therefore,
a compiled edition is not a Buddhist sutra, nor is it a stringing together of the words and phrases of sutras, but an exposition of the sutras
(the Sutra of Immeasurable Life)
and the spreading of them; hence
Master Ouyi praised it, saying:
"This is the wheel of Dharmakara's vows."
[The wheel of Dharmakara's vows]
Vastly delivering all sentient beings, causing them swiftly to be born in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The Bhikshu Dharmakara said:
"All you beings who transmigrate through the various destinies, be swiftly born in my land and receive bliss."
(from the Sutra of the Adornments of the Mahayana Immeasurable Life of the Buddha, the Song translation)
Below are the questions and answers.

1. The translating of sutras in ancient times was extremely cautious: translating Buddhist sutras was a most solemn undertaking; the scriptures translated were all weighed and verified collectively, and one could not "edit according to one's own fancy and propagate the Buddhist sutras".
[Note] A compiled edition is not a Buddhist sutra, so there is no question of "editing according to one's own fancy and propagating the Buddhist sutras".

[That a compiled edition is not a Buddhist sutra] A Buddhist sutra bears the name of its translator and is marked as a "translation"; a compiled edition bears the name of its compiler and is marked as "compiled".
The two must not be confused.

2. Compiling Buddhist sutras is extremely difficult to do without error: compiling Buddhist sutras is no easy matter; with all of Wang Longshu's attainments in Buddhist learning, he still could not avoid mistakes, and others would find it even harder to guarantee quality.

[Note] Although Xia Lianju was not necessarily wiser than Wang Longshu, because he stood on the shoulders of giants, developing strengths and discarding weaknesses, each later edition surpassed the earlier one, and his compiled edition clearly excels Wang's. This proves that it is not the case that "others would find it even harder to guarantee quality", and still less should one give up eating for fear of choking.
3. Compiling leads to reckless alteration of the sutras: compiling Buddhist sutras would set a precedent for later people to recklessly alter the Buddhist sutras at will.

[Note] A compiled edition is not a Buddhist sutra, so there is no question of "recklessly altering the Buddhist sutras at will". A compiled edition is simply a compiled edition: it is the use of refined and concise wording to
synthesize and expound
, and
spread
the contents of the five original translations, and it is not a Buddhist sutra. The two must be distinguished and must not be confused.

4. The ancient worthies did not circulate compiled editions: great masters of old such as Master Lianchi did not circulate compiled editions, and therefore other compiled editions must not be circulated today either.
[Note] To say that "the ancient worthies did not circulate compiled editions: great masters of old such as Master Lianchi did not circulate compiled editions" does not accord with the facts.
Master Lianchi said of the compiled edition:
Truly, it has been of great service to the Pure Land!
Master Ouyi
personally collated and engraved
Wang Longshu's compiled edition,
and wrote a preface in praise of it
It has circulated throughout the world for more than a thousand years
this shows that the compiled edition flourished without decline throughout the long ages
This is the wheel of Dharmakara's vows.
the Lingfeng Zonglun
Postface to the Engraved and Collated Great Amitābha Sutra
) And Master Yinguang, in
the Preface Urging Its Practice for the Re-engraving of the Brief Explanation of the Amitābha Sutra with the Perfectly Penetrating Commentary,
said:
"Youxi
(Master Youxi)
took it up
(the Wang compiled edition of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life)
because its wording and meaning are thorough and it circulates throughout the world
, and so he cited it in particular."
All of this proves that the compiled edition
(the Wang compiled edition)
circulated throughout the world down the long ages! And it has been of great service to the Pure Land school!

In his famous Commentary and Notes on the Amitābha Sutra, wherever Master Lianchi cites the Sutra of Immeasurable Life, he mostly quotes the compiled edition and only occasionally the original translations.
Master Youxi, in his famous Yuanzhong Commentary on the Amitābha Sutra, quotes the compiled edition throughout.
And
moreover Wang Longshu's compiled edition, the Great Amitābha Sutra, was
included in the Qianlong Tripitaka!
All of this
proves
that eminent monks of every generation alike circulated the compiled edition
"this is the wheel of Dharmakara's vows"
in order to spread the Dharma and save living beings. How then
can it be said that great masters of old such as Master Lianchi and Master Ouyi did not circulate compiled editions?
[That eminent monks of every generation alike circulated the compiled edition
"this is the wheel of Dharmakara's vows"
in order to spread the Dharma and save living beings]
The eminent monks'
insight was lofty and their doctrinal eye perfectly clear,
which only throws into sharper relief how those who oppose the compiling of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life
have shallow insight and a deluded doctrinal eye

5. Compiled editions give a handle to those who oppose Buddhism: compiling Buddhist sutras would give those who oppose Buddhism the pretext that "the Buddhist sutras were fabricated by later people and were not translated from India".
[Note] A compiled edition is not a Buddhist sutra at all, so this pretext does not exist.
Question: Did Master Yinguang say that the Sutra of Immeasurable Life may not be compiled?
Answer:
Master Yinguang
never said
that the Sutra of Immeasurable Life may not be compiled!
Rather, he held that the Sutra of Immeasurable Life may be compiled
See
Master Yinguang on the Compiled Edition
for details.
Question: Master Yinguang said:
"Since the Sutra of Immeasurable Life already exists, why make trouble where there is none?
I write this, on the one hand to show the difficulty of compiling, and on the other to put a stop to the recklessness of later people."
Is this not an opposition to compiling the Sutra of Immeasurable Life?
Answer:
"Since the Sutra of Immeasurable Life already exists, why make trouble where there is none"
has been
twisted by some, quoting out of context, into: since the original translations already exist, why go on to make trouble where there is none by compiling?
In fact, that is not at all what Master Yinguang meant.
This sentence is taken from the Collected Writings of Dharma Master Yinguang
the Third Reply to the Layman Wang Zili. Throughout this entire letter (
for the full letter, see
Master Yinguang on the Compiled Edition
, part three of that article
), Master Yinguang is speaking of the chief errors of the Wang Compiled Edition:
"rigidly insisting that the three grades are the nine classes
(rigidly insisting that what the Sutra of Immeasurable Life calls
the upper, middle, and lower grades are the upper three, middle three, and lower three classes of the nine classes in the Contemplation Sutra
, and is not at all discussing whether the Sutra of Immeasurable Life may be compiled. Judging from the theme of the whole letter and the context of this sentence,
"Since the Sutra of Immeasurable Life already exists, why make trouble where there is none"

means: since the true causes of rebirth in the upper, middle, and lower grades are already set forth in the Sutra of Immeasurable Life, why insist on making trouble where there is none by forcing them onto the
upper three, middle three, and lower three classes
of the nine classes in the Contemplation Sutra? (
see
Master Yinguang on the Compiled Edition
for details)

[Rigidly insisting that the three grades are the nine classes] In the original translations of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life, the upper, middle, and lower grades all arouse the bodhi mind, and so all are good people. Wang Longshu, however, mistakenly held that the upper, middle, and lower grades in the Sutra of Immeasurable Life are the upper three, middle three, and lower three classes of the nine classes in the Contemplation Sutra. But the lower three classes in the Contemplation Sutra are all evildoers. He therefore reasoned: since the lower grade consists of evildoers, how could evildoers arouse the bodhi mind? So the Wang Compiled Edition says:
"Those born in the lower grade cannot perform various meritorious deeds,
and do not arouse the mind of unsurpassed bodhi
This is an error of principle. Master Yinguang therefore criticized him in this letter, saying:
Therefore to take the lower grade as the lower three classes is a great error.

Hence for the upper grade he does not mention arousing the bodhi mind, for the middle grade he does mention arousing the bodhi mind, and for the lower grade he says no bodhi mind is aroused. Yet in the three grades of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life, all alike arouse the bodhi mind. Layman Wang thought that the lower grade, being deep in karmic offenses, could not arouse the bodhi mind; he did not consider that of the lower grade there is not a single word about committing karma, that they are in fact good people, and that they can only be the middle class of the nine classes.
To insist on making the lower grade the lower class
(this is precisely "making trouble where there is none")
, contravening the sutra and losing the principle, amounting in the end to arbitrarily altering the sutra; the fault is very great."
Moreover, if Master Yinguang had been saying
"since the original translations already exist, why go on to make trouble where there is none by compiling?"
then he would have written:
Since the original translations already exist
, why make trouble where there is none?"
and not:
Since the Sutra of Immeasurable Life already exists
, why make trouble where there is none?
For
"the Sutra of Immeasurable Life"
stands in contrast to
"the Contemplation Sutra"
, and at the very beginning of this letter Master Yinguang wrote:
In the Sutra of Immeasurable Life
there are three grades;
in the Contemplation Sutra
there are nine classes."
And
what stands in contrast to
the compiled edition"
should be
"the original translations
Pay particular attention to this:
If one takes
"Since the Sutra of Immeasurable Life already exists, why make trouble where there is none"

to mean "since the original translations already exist, why go on to make trouble where there is none by compiling?", then Master Yinguang would be rebuking Wang Longshu: he should never have compiled at all
, making trouble where there is none!
How could Master Yinguang, who praised Wang Longshu as
one who returned by the power of his vow"
(please note:
Master Yinguang says that Wang Longshu was a great bodhisattva who returned by the power of his vow
), rebuke Wang Longshu in such a way?
It was Master Lianchi who first pointed out what was not appropriate in Wang Longshu's compiled edition, and he deeply regretted it. That is to say, this compiled edition
satisfied a practical need in the study and practice of the Pure Land school
, yet still had points that were not appropriate. He did not rebuke Wang Longshu for making trouble and say that he should never have compiled at all! And he affirmed that this compiled edition is
"of great service to the Pure Land"
Master Lianchi said:
"The layman's compilation of the four translations
(the layman Wang Longshu's compilation of the four original translations)
is concise in wording and complete in meaning, smooth in phrasing and clear in principle.
Truly, it has been of great service to the Pure Land! It is to be regretted that
there is much in it that is not quite right
regrettably,
there is much in it that is not quite appropriate)
(from the Daily Recitation of Various Sutras)
This is the attitude of the Pure Land patriarchs toward compiled editions!

Therefore the task of later generations is: to correct what is not appropriate, to compile well this compiled edition that satisfies a practical need in the study and practice of the Pure Land school, and not to oppose compiling at all!

Moreover, the Wang Longshu compiled edition was indeed included in the Qianlong Tripitaka. Would Master Yinguang go so far as to denounce the eminent monks who reviewed and approved the Qianlong Tripitaka for being blind, for taking such superfluous and erroneous material into the canon? In particular, the Pure Land patriarch Master Ouyi even personally
collated and engraved
this compiled edition
, and wrote a preface praising it
“This is the wheel of Dharmakara’s vows.”

Would Master Yinguang denounce Master Ouyi’s “reckless deeds and reckless words (since the original translations already existed, why still collate, engrave, and circulate this compiled edition, and moreover
praise
“This is the wheel of Dharmakara’s vows.”
)”? How could Master Yinguang ever do that?! And now there are even people who, seeing the compiling together of the several original translations

(compiling these several original translations was for the sake of propagating the Sutra of Immeasurable Life, to help practitioners steep themselves in it so as to grasp the meaning of the sutra, deepen their faith and vows, and cultivate in accordance with the teaching; hence Master Ouyi
praised:
“This is the wheel of Dharmakara’s vows.”

, denounce it as “the arrogant presumption of a literatus of wisdom-karma”! This is truly judging a gentleman’s heart by the measure of a petty man. In their eyes, what kind of person has Wang Longshu become? These people are bold enough — do they not fear their transgression! This also shows how depraved and arrogant the hearts of people today have become!
I write this, on the one hand to show the difficulty of compiling, and on the other to put a stop to the recklessness of later people.”

, and some people quote it out of context and twist it into: writing these above words, on the one hand shows the difficulty of compiling, and on the other puts a stop to later people recklessly compiling the Sutra of Immeasurable Life again. In fact, what Master Yinguang meant by saying
“I write this, on the one hand to show the difficulty of compiling, and on the other to put a stop to the recklessness of later people”

is: writing these above words, on the one hand shows the difficulty of compiling, and on the other puts a stop to later people’s heedless view of rigidly equating the three grades with the nine classes of rebirth. And moreover
“I write this, on the one hand to show the difficulty of compiling”

these words also show that Master Yinguang was not opposed to compiling the Sutra of Immeasurable Life, but rather held that compiling is very difficult, and must be carried out by those capable of undertaking it.
This also
proves
that Master Yinguang considered it permissible to compile the Sutra of Immeasurable Life.
Because,
if Master Yinguang had considered compiling impermissible,
he would have said:
“I write this, on the one hand to show
that compiling is impermissible
rather than saying:
on the one hand to show
the difficulty of compiling
see
Master Yinguang on the Compiled Edition
And moreover, if
“Since the Sutra of Immeasurable Life already exists, why make trouble where there is none
means that compiling is impermissible, then the later words
I write this, on the one hand to show the difficulty of compiling.”
would certainly have been written as
“I write this, on the one hand to show
that compiling is impermissible
rather than saying
on the one hand to show
the difficulty of compiling
However, what Master Yinguang verifiably wrote was precisely:
on the one hand to show
the difficulty of compiling
How could Master Yinguang, a writer of such consummate skill, make so obvious an error of contradicting himself before and after? — for in the preceding text he had said it was
impermissible to compile
, and in the following text he again says
the difficulty of compiling
! Those who twist Master Yinguang’s instruction and claim that he opposed compiling the Sutra of Immeasurable Life are in truth slandering the Master!
Questioner: Master Yinguang criticized the compiled edition for
“altering the sutras and repudiating the ancients,”
so compiling is impermissible.
Answer: This is someone quoting out of context and twisting
“altering the sutras and repudiating the ancients,”
this phrase into saying that Master Yinguang meant: the compiled edition recklessly altered the sutra text (altering the sutras) and disparaged the original translations (repudiating the ancients).
In fact, that is not the case at all.
“Altering the sutras and repudiating the ancients,”

this phrase — in his letter “A Reply to a Letter from a Mr. of Yongjia,” Master Yinguang said: the book “A Frank Discussion of the Amitābha Sutra” must not be circulated, because it contains the problem of
“altering the sutras and repudiating the ancients.”

“Altering the sutras” means that A Frank Discussion of the Amitābha Sutra sought to replace the Sutra of Immeasurable Life spoken by the Buddha, translated by Kang Sengkai, with the Wei compiled edition; “repudiating the ancients” means that
the book’s author, Wang Gengxin,
in A Frank Discussion of the Amitābha Sutra, disparaged such patriarchs as Master Feixi, Master Lianchi, and Master Ouyi.
Therefore, Master Yinguang was criticizing A Frank Discussion of the Amitābha Sutra for
“altering the sutras and repudiating the ancients,”
not criticizing the compiled edition for
“altering the sutras and repudiating the ancients.”
[Altering the sutras] A Frank Discussion of the Amitābha Sutra says: the five original translations
“are none of them excellent editions.”
It also specifically criticizes the Sutra of Immeasurable Life spoken by the Buddha, translated by Kang Sengkai, saying of it:

“repetitious and prolix, ... hence the Sutra of Immeasurable Life, to this day, is not listed in the daily recitation of the monasteries. As a result, the great vow of our World-Honored Buddha — the causes fully including the fruit-sea, and the fruit penetrating the cause-source — is not made manifest
(in the older sense, the same as ‘manifest’)
in the world. Is this not a great regret for the scriptures and teachings of the Pure Land!”
And it praises the Wei compiled edition as
“this sutra
(the Sutra of Immeasurable Life)
at its crown,”
desiring to replace Kang Sengkai’s translation with the Wei compiled edition. [Repudiating the ancients] In the earlier part of this letter, Master Yinguang wrote:
“As for pointing out and disparaging Zige
(Master Feixi)
and Yunqi
(Master Lianchi)
and Ouyi and others, this only reveals their own shallowness of knowledge.”

Master Yinguang on the Compiled Edition
Questioner: Master Yinguang said:

How dare we circulate the Wei edition, so as to open the door for people to recklessly alter the Buddhist sutras, and for the stream of those who slander Buddhism, saying that the Buddhist sutras are all fabricated later by people, and were not originally translated from the Buddha-land.”
This says: the compiled edition recklessly altered the Buddhist sutras and fabricated them. So compiling is impermissible.
Answer: Master Yinguang’s
“How dare we
(we of our generation)

circulate the Wei edition, so as to open the door for people to recklessly alter the Buddhist sutras, and for the stream of those who slander Buddhism, saying that the Buddhist sutras are all fabricated later by people, and were not originally translated from the Buddha-land”
this instruction is a criticism directed at the fact that at that time some people were circulating the Wei compiled edition as though it were a sutra (without marking it as a compiled edition).
A compiled edition is a compiled edition, not a sutra. Just think: if the compiled edition already clearly bore the words “compiled edition” on its cover, how could it

“open the door for people to recklessly alter the Buddhist sutras, and for the stream of those who slander Buddhism, saying that the Buddhist sutras are all fabricated later by people, and were not originally translated from the Buddha-land”
Because a compiled edition is not a sutra to begin with, so there is no question of recklessly altering or fabricating a sutra.

Master Yinguang on the Compiled Edition

Question: The article “Reflections on the Phenomenon of Compiled Editions” circulates widely on the internet. It says: “Opposing compiled editions and promoting compiled editions represent a struggle on two fronts: relying on the Dharma versus relying on persons, and valuing the Three Jewels versus valuing a famous layman. Looking at the history of the development of the Pure Land school,
from the very day compiled editions came into being,
this frontline struggle has never been interrupted.” Is this true?

Answer: Those who say such things are only afraid that the world will not fall into chaos! This too is surely a manifestation of the fierce struggle of the Dharma-ending age. The extremely high praise that past patriarchs, cited above, lavished on Wang Longshu —
that is the sangha treasure praising a famous layman; where do you see any “struggle on two fronts between valuing the Three Jewels and valuing a famous layman”?!
Question: The article “Reflections on the Phenomenon of Compiled Editions” writes: “
Here I cite merely one example — Layman Xia Lianju’s unconscionable audacity in even daring to abridge and discard Amitābha Buddha’s great vows
, to illustrate this: in the Sutra of the Adornments of the Mahayana Immeasurable Life of the Buddha, translated by Dharma Master Faxian in the Song dynasty, the Bhikshu Dharmakara made a vow (the
vow) saying:

‘When I have attained bodhi and become fully enlightened, all sentient beings in the ten directions — in the immeasurable, boundless, countless worlds — who hear my name, arouse the bodhi mind, and plant various roots of goodness,
may, as they wish, be reborn in the Buddha-lands
, none fail to be reborn there; all of them shall be caused to attain Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.’
This shows that Amitābha Buddha was not only wishing everyone to go to his land, but follows the wishes of sentient beings
; this is the embodiment of utterly thorough compassion. As ordinary people, how could we ever conjecture the immeasurable wondrous functions of the Buddhas! But,
such an important vow
, in the Xia Lianju compiled edition, which claims to be the ‘most excellent edition’ of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life, has been deleted and no longer exists!”
My question is: is this
how
the Bhikshu Dharmakara made his great vow?
Answer: From
may, as they wish, be reborn in the Buddha-lands
” making the
“absurd conclusion that Amitābha Buddha was not only wishing everyone to go to his land, but follows the wishes of sentient beings,”
this is the author himself having mispunctuated the punctuation marks, and yet he comes to denounce Layman Xia Lianju for his unconscionable audacity!
Who, in the end,
is the one with unconscionable audacity?
The period between
“as they wish, be reborn
” and “
in the Buddha-lands
he did not punctuate out, and so read
“as they wish, be reborn
In the Buddha-lands
,” which he read as
“may, as they wish, be reborn in the Buddha-lands,”

turning the passage into an entirely different meaning: the Bhikshu Dharmakara made a vow that all sentient beings in the ten directions, “who hear my name, arouse the bodhi mind, and plant various roots of goodness,”
may, as they wish, be reborn in the Buddha-lands
, and moreover it must be ensured that the sentient beings reborn in those Buddha-lands become Buddhas
“all shall be caused to attain Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi
Good heavens!

How could Amitābha Buddha make such a great vow? Is this the meaning of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life? If so, do we sentient beings of this Sahā world still need to seek rebirth in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss? Amitābha Buddha, on the causal ground,
after passing through immeasurable, inconceivable, incalculable kalpas,
of indescribable toil
only then built the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss — what then is its meaning?

[Causal ground] From the ground of the ordinary person, when one first arouses the mind to study Buddhism, up to the time just before fully realizing Buddhahood — this entire process is called the “causal ground.”
In fact, the fourteenth vow of the Sutra of the Adornments of the Mahayana Immeasurable Life of the Buddha (the Song translation) is:

“World-Honored One, when I have attained bodhi and become fully enlightened, all sentient beings in the ten directions — in the immeasurable, boundless, countless worlds — who hear my name, arouse the bodhi mind, and plant various roots of goodness, may as they wish seek rebirth
(as they wish, seeking rebirth in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss)
in the Buddha-lands
(such sentient beings in the Buddha-lands)
, none fail to be reborn
(none fail to be reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss)
; all of them shall be caused to attain Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi.”
[Such sentient beings] Those who hear Amitābha Buddha’s name, arouse the bodhi mind, plant various roots of goodness, and seek rebirth in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.

Right in this translation (the Sutra of the Adornments of the Mahayana Immeasurable Life of the Buddha), Amitābha Buddha, when on the causal ground, before the Tathagata King of Sovereign Self-Existence,
“praised the Buddha with verses, his face majestic and serene. He again made his vast vows, and recited:
In all the boundless worlds
, the sentient beings transmigrating through the various destinies,
quickly be born in my land
and enjoy bliss; before long they shall together accomplish the unsurpassed way.’
Please note: it is “
quickly be born in my land
”! Where is there any “
may, as they wish, be reborn in the Buddha-lands

Question: The article “Fifty-Four Questions and Answers Arising from the Xia Lianju Compiled Edition of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life” says: “Compilation is a term for weaving and combining sutras, following one’s own mind and doing as one pleases, arbitrarily altering the sutras,
to use Master Yinguang’s words, it is the habitual conduct of the ‘arrogant presumption of a literatus of wisdom-karma’
.” Did Master Yinguang say this?
Answer:
This is fabrication!
Master Yinguang never said
“the arrogant presumption of a literatus of wisdom-karma”

these words; you may look them up in the Collected Writings of Dharma Master Yinguang. Fabricating a patriarch’s instruction out of thin air to deceive the masses is something one must take responsibility for,
and it is by no means what a disciple of the Buddha should do!
Although one may deceive those readers who never check against the original text, remember this:
three feet above your head, there are the gods!
[Literatus of wisdom-karma] In the Collected Writings of Dharma Master Yinguang, only in one place (the preface to An Easy Explanation of Learning Buddhism) is the word
“literatus of wisdom-karma”
used. In the preface to An Easy Explanation of Learning Buddhism, Master Yinguang wrote:
“Because
(owing to the fact that)
the Buddhist scriptures, commentaries, and treatises are profound in wording and deep in meaning. Even
(even though)
a literatus of wisdom-karma
who has long studied them would still find it hard to grasp their purport and enter their deep recesses; how much more so would the foolish men and women!”

[Deep recesses] The innermost part of an inner chamber; here used to liken the profound essence of the scriptures and treatises. [Wisdom-karma] The actions set in motion by wisdom, and the various good deeds done accordingly. “literatus of wisdom-karma”: one who both does good with wisdom and possesses very deep literary attainment.
This is a very painful lesson:

the reason evil doctrines are able to run rampant (for example, the Primal Vow Dharma-gate) is that their tactic is to tamper with, twist, and even fabricate sutras and the instructions of the patriarchs, and to quote sutras and the patriarchs’ instructions out of context, thereby deceiving the faithful: this is spoken by the Buddha, said by a patriarch, it is the holy word.

Thus the faithful, toward the views and theories of those evil doctrines, will readily believe them with deep conviction. Once they are deeply convinced, they will actively propagate, praise, and defend these evil doctrines (thinking they are spreading the Dharma and protecting the Dharma), and will further elaborate the views and theories of these evil doctrines (including inventing new stories), thereby forming a great force to wipe out the correct teaching.
[Holy word] This was spoken by a sage, is correct and reliable, and can certainly be believed and accepted.

In fact, these faithful who wave the flags and charge into battle are also themselves victims of the evil doctrine (how unjust!). For one may deceive people, deceive things, but it is hard to deceive Heaven; good and evil, when their end arrives, always have their retribution. Though these victims were deceived, it is still they themselves who experience the evil retribution!
In order to put an end to this great defect, the Buddhist community should establish a rule:

whenever one quotes sutras and the instructions of the patriarchs, or claims that this is spoken by the Buddha or said by a patriarch, one must quote the original text, or note the original text in parentheses, and indicate the source.
This way readers can check the original work to confirm whether the Buddha and the patriarchs indeed said so, and to confirm the accuracy of the quotation and its true meaning.
Question: The Sutra of Immeasurable Life has five original translations and four compiled editions; for daily study and practice, which one should one recite?

Answer: This depends on each person’s specific situation. Whichever edition is more helpful for you in grasping the meaning of the sutra and for steeping yourself in it, recite that one. Of course, you may also take turns reciting several editions. But whichever approach you take, the key is all the same:
grasp the meaning of the sutra
(the meaning of the Sutra of Immeasurable Life)
, deepen your faith and vows, and cultivate in accordance with the teaching.
Hold this firmly in mind:
Though one is diligent and diligent, whole life long, it is but a single instant; in the next life one is born in the Land of Immeasurable Life, with bliss beyond measure.
